correctness.rationale: Two independently constructed graph representations enumerate every vertex subset up to cardinality five. Globality criterion is proved. All four-and-smaller cases fail, five-set counts agree in two independent programs, non-global sets equal the exactly 96 five-subsets of neighborhoods, all possible jumps/slides are checked, all-distances computed in the bitmask program. Explicit checked automorphism permutations produce the reported orbit partitions. Execution outputs are embedded and all verification programs can be replayed from the embedded files.

value.rationale: The canonical nonisomorphic strongly regular pair has identical parameters (16,6,2,2) and spectrum, making a complete differing optimum-code enumerator a motivated counterexample to parameter-determined multiplicity. The exact difference of 384 codes and the full code-exchange/orbit profiles characterize naturally optimal identifying placements in both graphs, rather than an arbitrary unmotivated slice. The classification has graph-code and relocation implications without needing an infinite generalization.
